html:
The Battle of the Sutjeska was fought in May and June 1943 in the mountains of southeastern Bosnia, where German and Axis forces tried to encircle and destroy Tito's Partisan army.

About 120,000 Axis troops surrounded some 20,000 Partisans in rugged country along the Sutjeska River. Tito himself was wounded. The Partisans broke out to the northwest, but lost about a third of their men, and thousands of wounded left behind were killed. Surviving the battle convinced the Allies that the Partisans, not the royalist Chetniks, were the force fighting Germany in Yugoslavia, and Britain switched its support to them. A huge memorial stands at Tjentište in the valley.
sum: The Battle of the Sutjeska was fought in May and June 1943 in the mountains of southeastern Bosnia, where German and Axis forces tried to encircle and destroy Tito's Partisan army.
